Hi Marissa —

Thanks again for the demo last week. LaunchLab is finalizing cohort packages for startups joining in Aug/Sept and we'd like to include Redwood as our inference partner. Before we loop procurement, can you share how Redwood structures onboarding subsidies for accelerator partners?

Specifically:
- Do you offer a one-time onboarding credit or an ongoing discounted tier for cohort participants?
- Are there eligibility thresholds (e.g., company size, 12-month commit)?
- Typical timelines to get a private account / dedicated capacity set up?

I attached a draft SOW that outlines the cohort schedule and estimated consumption per startup (LaunchLab_SOW_v1.pdf). Procurement will want a clear billing/credit structure so we can include it in the partnership packet.

Would love your thoughts by EOD Wednesday so I can include it in our partner packet.

Hi Ana —

Great to hear — excited about the possibility of working with LaunchLab. Quick answers up front, then a proposed structure:

Short answers:
- We can do either a one-time onboarding credit or a time-limited discounted baseline; we usually combine both for accelerator partners.
- Typical eligibility: startups in an accelerator cohort enrolled within program dates; we don't require a revenue threshold but we do prefer an account owner (LaunchLab) to nominate participants.
- Private/Dedicated setup: 2–4 weeks for private account provisioning, quicker (3–7 days) for hosted API usage.

Proposed structure for your cohort (draft):
1) One-time onboarding subsidy: $10k in hosted credits per cohort cohort to be split across nominated startups (we can specify per-company caps).
2) Promotional usage tier: 30% discount on hosted API usage for the first 90 days post-onboarding for all cohort participants.
3) Optional pilot Dedicated window: if a startup requests dedicated capacity and commits to a 3-month reserved capacity, we can offer a 15% discount on the Dedicated rate for that commitment.

I've looped in Vivek (pricing) and Monica (partner ops) to confirm whether the one-time credit amount is viable for a program of ~20 startups and to surface any procurement constraints. If that looks good, I'll draft a short mutual action plan and a customer-facing quote + a DocuSign for signature.

Thoughts?

Best,
Marissa Cole

Marissa / Ana —

Thanks for the framing, Marissa. Quick internal take: the proposed $10k one-time pool is workable if we treat it as a program-level marketing commitment rather than individual credits (keeps accounting tidy). For a 20-startup cohort that implies up to $500 each if split evenly, which matches other accelerator programs we've piloted.

Recommendation (counter-proposal to balance cost & signal):
- Reduce the one-time onboarding pool to $7,500 (program-level), with a per-company cap of $750.
- Keep the promotional tier but tighten to a 25% discount for the first 60 days (instead of 90) to limit open-ended usage.
- Offer a Dedicated pilot discount as proposed but require a 3-month minimum commit for the discounted rate; we'll include a clear overage rate if reserved capacity is exceeded.

I attached a short spreadsheet with the cost math and sample splits (redwood_counter_terms.xlsx).

If LaunchLab is comfortable with the numbers, Marissa — can you confirm whether the cohort wants the one-time pool to be managed centrally by LaunchLab (you nominate startups and we invoice LaunchLab) or paid out as credits to each startup's account? Procurement will want that detail.

—Vivek

Thanks — this is helpful and aligns with internal expectations. Two quick notes from procurement:

2) Procurement asked for a formal quote and the SOW updated with the billing model (central pool + per-company cap).

Procurement is okay with the $7.5k pool + $750 cap and the 25% for 60 days as long as the SOW clearly lists the program-level terms and the Dedicated pilot minimums / overage policy.
